boundaryRepairs.before: And He commanded Noah to make him an
boundaryRepairs.evidence: Marginal 21 is beside the line beginning 'beasts, and fowls of the air, and that which moveth on the earth.' The proposed 'And He commanded Noah to' follows on that same line, and 'make him an ark' continues on the line bearing marginal 22. The proposed start is visible; there is no inline 21 at that point.

boundaryRepairs.before: Thus it is engraven and ordained on the
boundaryRepairs.evidence: The penultimate body line ends 'Thus it is engraven and ordained on the heavenly'; the final line bears marginal 31 and reads 'tablets. And there is no neglecting (this commandment) ...'. The 1913 wording is 'tablets', whereas the supplied 1917 candidate says 'tables'. Keep the 1913/CCEL wording; the marginal position alone cannot select between the two sentence starts.

boundaryRepairs.before: And in the seventh year of this week
boundaryRepairs.evidence: The seventh-year birth of Abram is adjacent to marginal verse 15; explicit 1917 numbering places the complete opening chronology in verse 15.

boundaryRepairs.before: And he said, 'What help and profit have
boundaryRepairs.evidence: Marginal 2 shares the line containing the end of 'Father!', 'And he said, Behold, here am I, my son', and a second 'And he said,' introducing the separately set poetic question. The proposed boundary at that second speech introduction fits the visible sequence but is not marked inline.

boundaryRepairs.before: And these words he spake to his two
boundaryRepairs.evidence: The line bearing marginal 8 contains 'cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay thee.' and ends with 'And'. The next line continues 'these words he spake to his two brothers ...' beside marginal 9. The proposed 'And these words' is intact across this line break; the print has no inline delimiter deciding the boundary.

boundaryRepairs.before: And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and
boundaryRepairs.evidence: 'And she bare him six sons, Zimram,' appears after 'for Hagar had died before Sarah' on the line above marginal 12. The line bearing 12 continues the sons' names through 'in the two weeks of years' and ends 'And in'. No wording in this proposed boundary window is absent, but the marker does not identify the sentence start inline.

boundaryRepairs.before: And in the sixth week, in the second
boundaryRepairs.evidence: The line bearing marginal 12 ends 'And in'; the line bearing 13 begins 'the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and'. The following line describes Jacob and Esau. The proposed opening is visible across the break, with 2046 A.M. printed in the right margin nearby.

boundaryRepairs.before: And they both went forth together from Abraham
boundaryRepairs.evidence: Marginal 30 is beside a line containing the end of 'thou the first-born son, and to the people alway', 'Go in peace, my son', and 'And they both went forth'. The line beside marginal 31 continues 'together from Abraham. And Rebecca loved Jacob ...'. This is another mixed-line placement rather than inline proof.

boundaryRepairs.before: And he drew near and kissed him, and
boundaryRepairs.evidence: Marginal 11 is beside the line 'alway. And do thou, my son, Jacob, draw near and kiss me. And he drew near and kissed him,'. The next line reads 'and he said:' before the poetic blessing. The proposed speech introduction is visible on that mixed line; the precise boundary relies on the explicit-numbering comparison.

boundaryRepairs.before: And Jacob said: 'Swear to me, this day
boundaryRepairs.evidence: Marginal 5 shares the line ending Esau's 'what profit to me is this birthright?', then 'And he said to Jacob: I give it to thee' and 'And Jacob said:'. The line bearing 6 begins 'Swear to me, this day, and he sware unto him. And Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and pottage'. The proposed start is intact at the end of the mixed line; there is no inline verse number.

boundaryMethod: The 1913 edition uses marginal verse numbers. The repairs below follow explicit 1917 numbering where the corresponding 1913 marginal layout and wording are compatible; they do not replace the 1913 text with 1917 wording. Page citations are printed pages; PDF physical pages are printed page + 18.

retainedBoundaries.reason: At the top of printed page 43, marginal 9 directly accompanies the separate poetic line 'Serve them not, nor worship them,'. 'But serve ye the most high God, and worship Him continually:' is the next line. Printed page 42 ends the preceding material with 'And all who trust in them, trust in nothing.' Unlike the mixed-line cases, the visible 1913 placement provides stronger support for retaining 'Serve them not' within 20:9. It does not independently verify moving that line into 20:8 as the 1917 candidate proposes.
retainedBoundaries.decision: Retain CCEL/1913 start: Serve them not, nor worship them. Do not adopt the differing 1917 boundary.
